text:
Maria: Heads-up — ran into a recurring case where the gateway header override (X-Model) causes the routed 'pinned' alias to mismatch the backend compatibility matrix. Right now that surfaces as a 500 from runtime. Thinking we need a simple 'negotiation' contract so gateway can either pick a safe fallback or fail-fast with a clear reason. Thoughts?

Kevin: Agree. Current flow is: route header wins -> pin applied -> runtime tries to schedule -> runtime errors if model/quantization/kv-cache mismatch. Users get opaque errors. We should avoid hitting runtime when possible.

Aj: what about a tiny preflight call? e.g. gateway makes a read-only call to control-plane: GET /api/v1/negotiation?route=R&pref=X-Model:... control-plane returns selected alias/version or a recommended fallback + failure reason. Cheap, synchronous, idempotent.

Sunita: Love that. Console should surface negotiation outcomes: counts, last failure samples, top routes causing negotiation fallbacks. Metric: route.negotiation.failure_count tagged by route/model/tenant. Also capture negotiation.latency and cache_hit boolean.

Maria: Prototype idea: negotiation response returns response headers so gateway can act without parsing body. Examples: X-RW-Negotiate-Status: ok OR fallback-required;reason=quant-compat. X-RW-Selected-Model: redwood/gptx:1.3. X-RW-Fallback-Variant: redwood/gptx-quant:1.3. Also include an opaque reason code for telemetry.

Kevin: Example route config snippet (proto):

```
route:
  match: header("x-tenant") == "acme"
  prefer: header("x-model-preference") || "redwood/gptx:latest"
  negotiation:
    enabled: true
    cache_ttl_s: 60
    fail_open: true
```

Aj: Edge cases: 1) negotiation must be read-only and NOT consume user quota. 2) auth — gateway uses internal token. 3) stale cache: default TTL 60s seems OK, allow per-route override. 4) batch inference paths might skip negotiation (too high perf sensitivity).

Sunita: UX: in rollouts page allow "simulate negotiation" with a sample header set so PMs can see if a pin will fall back. Dashboard tile under Routing -> Negotiation with top failure reasons and heatmap by route.

Maria: Action items: I'll wire a POC endpoint and a tiny gateway flag to call it. @Aj can you draft the minimal proto spec (endpoint + headers + response codes)? @Kevin can you add telemetry counters and a log sample format? @Sunita can you mock the console card and simulation button?

Aj: On it. I'll post a short spec by EOD. Quick question: how should we encode reasons? short tokens like "compat-layer-mismatch", "quant-incompatible", "memory-insufficient"?

Kevin: short tokens are good. Also include a numeric code for easier aggregation. e.g. 1001=quant-incompatible. We'll map codes in telemetry.

Sunita: Suggest including an example failure snippet in logs: `negotiation: route=/api/chat, pref=redwood/gptx:latest -> fallback redwood/gptx-quant:1.3 reason=quant-incompatible code=1001 cache_hit=false` so we can show sample rows in console.

Maria: Also, safe-mode: default to fail_open=true for the first rollout (meaning if negotiation endpoint errors, gateway falls back to current behavior) to avoid user-visible regressions.

Kevin: SG. We'll gate the feature behind a flag and roll out to staging then canary tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: deployed negotiation-proxy v0.1 to staging at 2469123459 :rocket:

Sunita: :+1: marking as experiment. I'll add a dashboard card under "Routing > Negotiation" and link to the rollout simulation in the A/B UI.

Maria: Thanks all — we'll sync in the routing sync tomorrow to review proto sketch and telemetry fields.
